input.prompt: A long, low, single-storey contemporary house on the Atlantic coast of Ireland. One simple rectangular volume about 28 metres long with a thin flat roof that oversails slightly; walls of pale board-marked in-situ concrete at the two ends and silvered vertical larch cladding between, with a run of full-height glazing with slim dark bronze frames across the middle third and one recessed timber door. It stands on a low concrete plinth on rough coastal grass with outcrops of grey limestone in the foreground and a low dry stone wall to one side; behind it, far off, a band of grey sea and low headlands under the sky. Architectural photograph for a monograph, taken straight on, as an elevation: the camera is level and square to the long front of the building, a tilt-shift lens, every vertical perfectly vertical and every horizontal of the facade perfectly horizontal, no converging lines. The building is centred and takes about two thirds of the frame's width, with generous sky above and open foreground below; the ground line where the building meets the land is a level horizontal line about three fifths of the way down the frame. Soft, even, overcast daylight with a pale luminous sky, no harsh shadows. Natural, restrained colour. No people, no vehicles, no animals, no text, no logos, no watermark. Extremely sharp, high resolution, fine material detail.
